style: Square card illustration for a historical strategy game, like the building cards of a Total War settlement panel. One single structure seen from above at a three-quarter oblique angle (about 40 degrees down), centred and large, filling about two thirds of the square, on a small patch of ground or shore; the surroundings fade softly into dark misty shadow toward all four edges and corners, a vignette with no hard border. Dark, moody hand-painted cinematic look: blue-hour dusk, deep navy water, dark pines, warm lantern and fire light, soft mist; the structure itself is clearly lit by warm torchlight with a cool moonlit rim so its shape reads at a small size, fine film grain, rich but desaturated colours. Painterly realism like a concept painting for a historical naval epic. Tiny figures are dark unrecognizable silhouettes, no faces. Absolutely no text, no letters, no Chinese characters, no Korean script, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no border, no frame, no UI, no modern objects, no rising-sun flag, no sunburst.

factions.joseon: Joseon Korea, 1590s: grey ceramic-tiled roofs with gently upturned eaves, white plastered walls and dark timber frames, grey fieldstone, plain blue and white cloth banners without any emblem.
factions.japan: Sengoku Japan, 1590s: black-lacquered timber, white plastered walls, dark grey tiled roofs, steep battered stone walls, plain white cloth banners without any emblem or marking.
factions.ming: Ming China, 1590s: grey brick walls, red lacquered timber, yellow and green glazed tiled roofs with sweeping ridges, plain red and yellow cloth banners without any emblem.
